post.instagram_caption:
"Macs can't get viruses" is a myth, and Apple's own software chief said so in court.

In 2021, during the Epic v. Apple trial, Craig Federighi testified: "We have a level of malware on the Mac that we don't find acceptable." He said Apple found about 130 kinds of Mac malware in a single year (CNBC). Macs do ship with built-in antivirus called XProtect (Apple).

Today many Mac threats don't break in, they trick you in, like fake pages that ask you to paste a command into Terminal (Macworld).

The lesson: keep macOS updated and only install apps from sources you trust.

Source: CNBC, May 19, 2021; Apple Platform Security; Macworld, Aug 2026.

Did you grow up believing Macs were virus-proof?

post.youtube_description:
"Macs can't get viruses" is a myth. In 2021, Apple's software chief Craig Federighi told a court that Apple had a level of Mac malware it didn't find acceptable, and that Apple found about 130 kinds of Mac malware in one year. Macs do include built-in antivirus called XProtect, but many threats now rely on tricking people, like fake pages asking you to paste a command into Terminal.

Sources:
• CNBC, "Apple's head of software says current level of Mac malware is not acceptable" (May 19, 2021)
• Apple Platform Security, "Protecting against malware in macOS"
• Macworld, "Do Macs need antivirus in 2026?" (Aug 28, 2026)
